Senses.Explanation: Letting out one line: the master's single thread of allowance out of the shut gate — the entry road granted, and then weighed against the holding-shut. Yuanwu Keqin rules on the oldest case of it: Yaoshan Weiyan said that at Shitou Xiqian's place he was like a mosquito on an iron ox — and the crowd explains it: Shitou always stood sheer as a ten-thousand-fathom wall, so he did not get it; Mazu Daoyi let out one line, and he woke — yet Yuanwu pulls the rug: Shitou's saying had already leaked, and Mazu's move is the more poisonous still; Linquan Conglun, on Yantou Quanhuo's word that Deshan Xuanjian's backbone was iron that would not break, says it plainly — letting out one line allows deliberation — and then grades it: better one foot walked than ten feet talked, one inch walked than one foot talked; Wanru Tongwei holds the fifteenth day — heaven is heaven, earth is earth, monk is monk, layman is layman, nothing lacking by a hair — so why do ten out of five pairs not know where it falls? Ruru will let out one line to give them an entry road; Yuan'an Liao, taking the room for the new elder: buddhas cannot get a foot in, demons find no door to peer through — today one line is let out: you have half a jin, I return you eight liang. Baishan Dekai splits it by the day — yesterday the border was sealed, today one line is let out: ice-floes in the boiling pot, lightning snatched in the flint-spark; meet it here and the work may knit into one piece, miss it and the pit waits; Zisu Chaoyuan plays the two ends: sometimes the ford is held shut and the mouths of three ages of buddhas hang on the wall; one line let out and the cats and calves run wherever they please — and the neither-holding-nor-releasing line, no one on earth can lay a finger on it; Yinyuan Longqi verses it: long sunk in dead water and hated for it, heaven and earth flipped over — ever woken? the season has come and will not be held back: one line let out, soaring free — but let the no-face fellow bar the way and demand the travel pass; Lianyue Daozheng turns the request inside out: the monk says to loose another's knots one must let out one line — the master: don't let yourself be caged; the monk: I take no cage — the master: then why do you want one line out? A shout. Binding yourself with no rope.
